findings.title: Variable detection strips only the unspaced {{RAW}}/{{END_RAW}} spelling, so the f1 fix misses tag forms the lexer accepts and the living doc documents

serves.scenario: The lexer opens a block on any tag whose trimmed content is RAW and closes it on /\{\{[ \t]*END_RAW[ \t]*\}\}/, and the living doc tells users the closing tag may be written {{ END_RAW }}. extractAllVariables removes only the exact text {{RAW}}...{{END_RAW}}. A node template such as '{{RAW}}${{name}}{{ END_RAW }}' or '{{ RAW }}${{name}}{{END_RAW}}' renders literally in the lexer, but detection still reports 'name'; with Strict Mode on (the default) and no mapping the node raises a missing-variable error, so the template still cannot carry tag-like text in the node. A lesser side effect of the same text-level regex: a literal {{RAW}} inside a comment, followed later by a real block, makes detection drop every variable in between, so Strict Mode would stop flagging them.

findings.rubric: goal-critical question 1: does everything between RAW and END_RAW come out exactly as written, including double braces and tag-like text (in the n8n node, per the project goal)
findings.reproduction: Call extractAllVariables('{{RAW}}${{name}}{{ END_RAW }}') and extractAllVariables('{{ RAW }}${{name}}{{END_RAW}}'). Expected [] for both; the regex at utils.ts:18 does not match either, so the result is ['name']. In the node: Template '{{RAW}}${{name}}{{ END_RAW }}', no mappings, Strict Mode on; expected output '${{name}}', failure is a missing-variable error. Smallest fix: use the lexer's tag shapes in the strip regex, for example /\{\{\s*RAW\s*\}\}[\s\S]*?\{\{[ \t]*END_RAW[ \t]*\}\}/g, and add these two cases to test-node/raw-block-review.test.ts.
